title: Real-time Binge-eating and Overweight Oxygenation Training (REBOOT) - Advancing food-specific near-infrared spectroscopy neurofeedback for binge-eating disorder
summary:
People with binge-eating disorder experience recurrent binge-eating episodes in which they lose control over eating. Studies suggest that certain brain regions involved in behavioral and impulse control may be less active in affected individuals in such situations.
This study investigates whether people with this condition can learn to specifically activate this brain region when their own brain activity is shown to them on a screen (neurofeedback training). It also examines how well such training can be carried out and how well it is accepted by participants.
Six women with binge-eating disorder take part. They wear a cap that uses light to detect changes in blood oxygenation in the front part of the brain. These changes can be used to infer brain activity. While looking at pictures of food, they receive feedback on their brain activity on a screen and practice upregulating it. To find out whether this feedback actually helps regulate brain activity, one of the two training phases uses prerecorded feedback instead of the participants’ actual brain activity.  Each participant completes the training both with feedback from her own brain activity and with the prerecorded feedback – in random order and without knowing at the time which variant she is receiving. Before, between, and after the training phases, the number of binge-eating episodes and participants' general wellbeing are assessed, among other measures.
conditions: Binge-eating disorder (BED) according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th Edition (DSM-5)

interventions.name: Group A (sham feedback in the first training phase): Participants first complete a 3-week baseline phase without intervention. They then receive six sessions of food-specific sham neurofeedback (control condition; prerecorded feedback that does not reflect the participant's actual brain activity) ov

Group B (active feedback in the first training phase): Participants first complete the same 3-week baseline phase without intervention. They then receive six sessions of active food-specific rtfNIRS-neurofeedback (intervention condition; real-time feedback of their own prefrontal brain activity) ove

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Binge-eating disorder according to DSM-5 with ≥ 4 objective binge-eating episodes/week
• BMI 25.0–44.9 kg/m²
• Written informed consent
• Sufficient German language skills
• Feasible commute to the treatment center
Exclusion criteria:
• Serious somatic conditions (e.g., neurological disorders, stroke, head injury)
• Severe mental disorders (e.g., psychotic disorder, suicidality, substance use disorder, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, developmental or intellectual disability)
• Previous or planned bariatric surgery
• Medication affecting eating behavior or executive functioning (e.g., antipsychotics)
• Smoking
• Ongoing psychotherapy
• Pregnancy or lactation
• Shift work
• Current participation in any weight loss treatment
• Uncorrected hearing or vision impairment
